## Summary
- Diagnostic Category: [`lint/nursery/useFencedCodeLanguage`](/reference/diagnostics#diagnostic-category)
- This rule doesn't have a fix.
- The default severity of this rule is [**information**](/reference/diagnostics#information).
- Sources: 
  - Same as [`fenced-code-language`](https://github.com/DavidAnson/markdownlint/blob/main/doc/md040.md)

## How to configure
```json title="biome.json"
{
	"linter": {
		"rules": {
			"nursery": {
				"useFencedCodeLanguage": "error"
			}
		}
	}
}

```
## Description
Enforce that fenced code blocks specify a code tag (language).

Renderers can use a code tag to select syntax highlighting when they support the language.
Use `text` for snippets when syntax highlighting is unwanted or unsupported.

## Options

The following options are available.

### `allowedLanguages`

A list of language tags fenced code blocks are allowed to declare. When empty (the
default), any language tag is accepted. Language tags are matched case-sensitively.

Default: `[]`

```json title='biome.json'
{
	"linter": {
		"rules": {
			"nursery": {
				"useFencedCodeLanguage": {
					"level": "on",
					"options": {
						"allowedLanguages": [
							"js",
							"ts"
						]
					}
				}
			}
		}
	}
}

```

```md
```python
print(1)
```
```

### `languageOnly`

When `true`, requires the info string to contain exactly the language tag, without
metadata or other non-whitespace content.

Default: `false`

```json title='biome.json'
{
	"linter": {
		"rules": {
			"nursery": {
				"useFencedCodeLanguage": {
					"level": "on",
					"options": {
						"languageOnly": true
					}
				}
			}
		}
	}
}

```

```md
```js startLine=3
console.log(1)
```
